title: Which angle sits between the two sides?
description: A corner where sides of six and five centimetres meet shows an angle of thirty degrees. The two arms of the angle are checked against the two given sides, then the angle is moved to the other end of the six centimetre side. Keeko's doubt is that any angle touching the six centimetre side counts as between the sides.
teaching_notes: One idea: an angle is included only when both of its arms are the two given sides. Watch for students who accept any angle that touches one of the given sides.

source: A triangle has two sides of 6 cm and 5 cm that meet at a corner, and the angle at that corner is 30°.
video_script.why: The child knows the sides and angles of a triangle but has not yet seen which angle sits between two given sides.
video_script.substitution: The book's own sides of six and five centimetres with an angle of thirty degrees.
video_script.anchor: a triangle corner where the sides of six and five centimetres meet at an angle of thirty degrees
video_script.wrong_answer: any angle that touches the six centimetre side counts as included
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko accepts the angle at the far end of the six centimetre side because it touches that side, but its other arm is a side that was not given.
video_script.payoff_line: Thirty degrees is the included angle only when it sits between the six and five centimetre sides

final_answer.spoken: yes, thirty degrees is included between the six and five centimetre sides, and at the other end it is not

maths_rules: the sides 6 cm and 5 cm meet at one corner, and the angle at that corner has those two sides as its two arms
so 30° is between the two given sides: it is the included angle
at the other end of the 6 cm side the angle has the 6 cm side as one arm and a side that is not given as the other arm
so that angle is not between the two given sides
video_script.design: One triangle corner drawn once and kept all video. The two given sides are coloured, the angle arc is marked at the corner, then the arc moves to the far end of the six centimetre side.

<bookmark mark='sides'/>Two of its sides are six centimetres and five centimetres long, and they meet at a corner.
<bookmark mark='angle'/>The angle at that corner is thirty degrees.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Is thirty degrees the angle between the two sides?

narration: <bookmark mark='arms'/>Every angle at a corner of a triangle has two arms, and each arm is a side.
<bookmark mark='name'/>An angle whose two arms are the two given sides is called the included angle.

beats.on_screen: Given: sides 6 cm and 5 cm meet at a corner; the angle at that corner is 30°

The angle there is thirty degrees.

beats.on_screen: To find: is 30° between the two sides? What if 30° is at the other end of the 6 cm side?

marks.find: the two questions are written under the given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find whether this angle is the included angle.
We also ask what changes at the other end of the six centimetre side.

narration: <bookmark mark='arms'/>Step one, name the two arms of the angle. One arm is the six centimetre side, and the other arm is the five centimetre side.

narration: <bookmark mark='between'/>Step two, compare the arms with the given sides. Both arms are given sides, so the angle lies between them.

<bookmark mark='arms'/>One arm is the six centimetre side, but the other arm is a side we were not given.

narration: <bookmark mark='cross'/>Step four, check the arms again. Only one arm is a given side, so this angle is not between the two.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 30° is the included angle at the corner of the 6 cm and 5 cm sides; at the other end it is not

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Thirty degrees is the included angle only when it sits between the six and five centimetre sides.
<bookmark mark='other'/>At the other end of the six centimetre side, it is not.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks any angle that touches the six centimetre side counts as included.
<bookmark mark='far'/>Look at the far end of that side. One arm is the six centimetre side, but the other arm is a different side.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Both arms must be the two given sides, so that angle does not count.
